tagline: Edit videos for creators and businesses — start earning with just a phone.
prerequisites: Willingness to learn CapCut or DaVinci Resolve

tasks: Download CapCut and edit a 30-second practice video using free stock footage
Create an Upwork profile with the headline 'Video Editor for TikTok & YouTube'
DM 3 small TikTok creators offering to edit one video for free

summary.description: Every business and creator needs video content, but most don't want to edit it themselves. Filipino video editors are in high demand because of competitive rates and strong English skills. You can start with short-form edits (TikTok, Reels) using free tools, then move to long-form YouTube editing as your skills grow.
who_is_this_for: People who enjoy watching and creating video content
TikTok or YouTube users who want to monetize their screen time
Anyone with patience for detail-oriented work
Students looking for a creative side income

reality_check.honest_assessment: Short-form editing (TikTok/Reels) is the fastest entry point — you can learn CapCut in a weekend. But it's competitive and pays less (₱200–₱500/video). Long-form YouTube editing pays ₱2,000–₱10,000/video but requires more skill. Expect to edit 5–10 free or cheap videos before landing consistent paid work.
reality_check.what_beginners_underestimate: How long editing actually takes. A 30-second TikTok can take 1–2 hours when you're learning. A 10-minute YouTube video can take 6–8 hours. Speed comes with practice, but your first month will feel painfully slow.
reality_check.why_people_fail: They spend weeks watching tutorials without editing real videos. Or they quote professional rates with a beginner portfolio and get zero responses. Or they take on too many projects, miss deadlines, and lose clients permanently.
reality_check.how_to_avoid_failure: Edit a real video every single day for your first 2 weeks — even if nobody asked you to. Start with free or low-cost edits to build your portfolio fast. Only take on projects you can finish within the deadline, even if it means saying no to money.

roadmap.title: Learn the Basics
roadmap.why: You need baseline editing skills before anyone will trust you with their content. This phase gives you the muscle memory to edit confidently.

steps.detail: Phone: CapCut (free). Laptop: DaVinci Resolve (free). Don't buy software — free tools are professional-grade.
steps.outcome: You have a professional editing tool installed and ready to use.

steps.detail: Download free stock footage from Pexels. Edit a 30-second TikTok, a 60-second Reel, and a 5-minute YouTube-style video. Focus on cuts, text overlays, and music.
steps.outcome: You understand the basic workflow: import, cut, add text/music, export.

steps.action: Watch 2 YouTube tutorials on your chosen tool
steps.detail: Search '[tool name] editing tutorial for beginners.' Learn keyboard shortcuts — they double your speed.
steps.outcome: You learn shortcuts and techniques that save hours on every future edit.

roadmap.title: Build Your Portfolio
roadmap.why: No client will hire you without proof you can edit. Free edits for small creators are the fastest way to get real samples.

steps.action: Edit 3 videos for small creators for free
steps.detail: Find TikTok creators with 1K–10K followers in your niche. DM: 'I'll edit your next 3 videos for free as portfolio pieces.' Most will say yes.
steps.outcome: You have real client work in your portfolio — not just practice edits with stock footage.

steps.detail: Upload your best 5 edits to a Google Drive folder or create a simple Carrd.co page (free) with video links.
steps.outcome: You have a shareable portfolio link to include in every proposal and DM.

steps.action: Set up profiles on Fiverr and Upwork
steps.detail: Fiverr gig: 'I will edit your TikTok or YouTube video.' Upwork profile: highlight turnaround speed and specific editing styles.
steps.outcome: Your freelance profiles are live and clients can find you through search.

roadmap.milestone: Portfolio with 5+ sample edits and freelance profiles live

roadmap.title: Get Paying Clients
roadmap.why: Free edits prove your skills, but paid work proves your business. This phase turns your portfolio into actual income.

steps.action: Send 5 proposals per day on Upwork
steps.detail: Filter for 'video editor' posted in last 24 hours. In your proposal, mention the client's content specifically — generic proposals get ignored.
steps.outcome: You're actively competing for paid work and improving your proposal game daily.

steps.action: Pitch creators directly on social media
steps.detail: Find YouTubers or TikTokers who post good content with poor editing. DM with a sample re-edit of their video.
steps.outcome: You bypass job boards and land clients who didn't even know they needed an editor.

steps.detail: Search 'video editor hiring PH' or 'Filipino video editors.' Post your portfolio. Respond to job posts within 1 hour.
steps.outcome: You tap into the Filipino freelancer network where many editors find their first recurring clients.

roadmap.title: Scale and Specialize
roadmap.why: General editors compete on price. Specialists compete on value — and value pays 2–3x more.

steps.detail: Specializing in one content type (podcasts, gaming, business) lets you charge more and edit faster. 'Podcast video editor' beats 'video editor' in every proposal.
steps.outcome: You stand out from thousands of general editors and attract clients willing to pay premium rates.

steps.detail: Tell repeat clients: 'I'll edit 8 videos/month for ₱X.' Retainers give you predictable income.
steps.outcome: You have predictable monthly income instead of hustling for every single project.

steps.detail: After Effects or Canva animations. Adding intros, lower thirds, and transitions increases your rate by 50–100%.
steps.outcome: You can offer premium editing services that justify ₱5,000–₱10,000 per video.

income_paths.title: Short-Form Video Editing (TikTok/Reels)
income_paths.detail: Edit 30–90 second videos for creators and brands. High volume, fast turnaround. Most accessible entry point.
income_paths.best_for: Complete beginners who want to start earning within 2 weeks — low barrier, high volume
income_paths.typical_beginner_mistake: Spending 3 hours perfecting a ₱300 edit — speed matters more than perfection for short-form content

income_paths.title: YouTube Video Editing
income_paths.detail: Edit long-form content (10–30 minutes) for YouTubers. Higher pay per video, requires more skill in pacing and storytelling.
income_paths.best_for: Editors who enjoy storytelling and are willing to invest time learning pacing, B-roll, and audio mixing
income_paths.typical_beginner_mistake: Not watching enough of the creator's existing content before editing — you need to match their style, not impose yours

income_paths.title: Business & Marketing Videos
income_paths.detail: Edit ads, product demos, and corporate videos. Businesses pay premium rates for professional-looking content.
income_paths.best_for: Editors with a clean, professional style who understand marketing — this pays the most but requires business communication skills
income_paths.typical_beginner_mistake: Using trendy editing styles (jump cuts, memes) in corporate videos — businesses want clean, professional, brand-aligned content

income_paths.title: Podcast Video Editing
income_paths.detail: Edit video podcasts — syncing audio, adding captions, cutting dead air. Growing niche with recurring work.
income_paths.best_for: Patient editors who enjoy audio work — podcasts are repetitive but provide the most stable recurring income
income_paths.typical_beginner_mistake: Not learning basic audio editing — podcast editors who can clean up audio are 2x more valuable than those who only do video cuts

platforms.name: Upwork
platforms.why: Best for finding international clients who pay in USD. Filter for 'video editor' and sort by recent posts.

platforms.name: Fiverr
platforms.why: Good for short-form editing gigs. Clients come to you. Start with low prices to build reviews.

platforms.name: OnlineJobsPH
platforms.why: Filipino employers often hire full-time remote video editors. Stable income with local bank payments.

platforms.name: Twitter/X
platforms.why: Many YouTube creators post 'looking for an editor' on Twitter. Follow creators in your niche and engage with their content.

tools.name: CapCut
tools.purpose: Best free editor for short-form content. Works on phone and desktop.
tools.why_it_matters: This is the industry standard for TikTok/Reels editing. Clients expect you to know it. You can start earning with just this one tool.
tools.when_to_start: Day 1 — download and edit your first practice video today

tools.name: DaVinci Resolve
tools.purpose: Professional-grade desktop editor. Free version has everything you need for client work.
tools.why_it_matters: When you're ready for long-form YouTube and business editing, this is what professionals use. It's free and rivals paid software costing ₱30,000+.
tools.when_to_start: Week 3 — after you've mastered short-form and want to take on YouTube clients

tools.name: Pexels
tools.purpose: Free stock video footage for practice projects and portfolio pieces.
tools.why_it_matters: You need footage to practice with before you have real clients. Pexels gives you unlimited material to build skills without waiting.
tools.when_to_start: Day 1 — download footage for your first practice edit

tools.name: Google Drive
tools.purpose: Share large video files with clients. 15GB free storage.
tools.why_it_matters: Clients need to send you raw footage and receive finished edits. Google Drive is the simplest way — no sign-up needed on their end.
tools.when_to_start: Day 1 — set up your file delivery system

tools.name: Canva
tools.purpose: Create thumbnails and simple motion graphics to add to video deliverables.
tools.why_it_matters: Editors who deliver a video plus a thumbnail charge 20–30% more. Canva makes thumbnail creation a 5-minute add-on.
tools.when_to_start: After your first 5 paid projects — add it as a value-add to increase your rates

faq.question: Can I start video editing on my phone?
faq.answer: Yes. CapCut on a smartphone is enough for short-form editing (TikTok, Reels). For YouTube-length videos, you'll eventually need a laptop — but you can earn your first income on a phone.

faq.question: Do I need a powerful computer?
faq.answer: Not for short-form. For long-form YouTube editing, a laptop with 8GB RAM and an SSD is the minimum. A secondhand ThinkPad (₱8,000–₱15,000) handles DaVinci Resolve well.

faq.question: How long does it take to edit a 10-minute YouTube video?
faq.answer: Beginners: 4–8 hours. Experienced editors: 2–3 hours. Speed comes from keyboard shortcuts, templates, and knowing your editing software well.

faq.question: What's the difference between short-form and long-form editing?
faq.answer: Short-form (TikTok/Reels) is fast cuts, trending audio, and text overlays. Long-form (YouTube) is pacing, b-roll, transitions, and audio mixing. Start with short-form, graduate to long-form.

faq.question: Is video editing still a good career with AI tools?
faq.answer: Yes. AI tools speed up tasks like captioning and color correction, but creative editing — pacing, storytelling, knowing what to cut — is still human work. Editors who use AI as a tool are faster, not replaced.
